subject: maths
question: A train, 250 m long, passes a railway platform 200 m long, in 45 s with a uniform speed. What is the time (in seconds) taken by the train to pass a man cycling in the direction of the train at a speed of 6 km/h?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Speed of train = Total Distance ÷ Time = (250 + 200) ÷ 45 = 10 m/s.

Speed of man = 6 × (5 ÷ 18) = 5/3 m/s.

Relative speed in same direction = 10 − 5/3 = 25/3 m/s.

Time to pass the man = Train Length ÷ Relative Speed = 250 ÷ (25/3).

Time = 250 × (3 ÷ 25) = 30 seconds.

**∴ The correct answer is 30 s.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of train = 250 m

Length of platform = 200 m

Time taken to cross platform = 45 s

Speed of man = 6 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

Relative Speed (Same Direction) = Speed of Train − Speed of Object

Time to cross a moving object = Train Length ÷ Relative Speed

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total distance covered to cross the platform = Length of train + Length of platform

⇒ Total distance = 250 + 200 = 450 m

⇒ Speed of train = 450 ÷ 45 = 10 m/s

⇒ Speed of man in m/s = 6 × (5 ÷ 18) = 5/3 m/s

⇒ Relative speed = 10 − 5/3 = (30 − 5) ÷ 3 = 25/3 m/s

⇒ Time taken to cross the man = Length of train ÷ Relative speed

⇒ Time = 250 ÷ (25/3) = (250 × 3) ÷ 25

⇒ Time = 10 × 3 = 30 s

**∴ The correct answer is 30 s.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed

When two objects move in the same direction, Relative Speed = S₁ − S₂. When they move in opposite directions, Relative Speed = S₁ + S₂.

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

Train Crossing Rules

When a train crosses a stationary object with length (platform, bridge), distance = Lₜᵣₐᵢₙ + Lₒbjₑ꜀ₜ. When it crosses a point object (man, pole), distance = Lₜᵣₐᵢₙ.
